nodes.name: Solvothermal Ni-ZIF-8 synthesis
nodes.procedure: By the solvothermal reaction of Zn²⁺, Ni²⁺, and 2-methylimidazole, Ni-doped ZIF-8 (Ni-ZIF-8) with an identical crystalline structure and morphology to the pristine ZIF-8 has been constructed successfully.
nodes.source_text: By the solvothermal reaction of Zn²⁺, Ni²⁺, and 2-methylimidazole... has been constructed successfully (Figure 1a, S1 and S2).

nodes.name: Microwave pyrolysis with ZnCl₂
nodes.procedure: To enhance the microwave absorption ability, ZnCl₂, a polar compound with strong microwave absorption capacity, is selected as the microwave absorber to mix with Ni-ZIF-8... the mixture of Ni-ZIF-8 and ZnCl₂ presents obvious microwave absorption and Ni-ZIF-8 is successfully carbonized within 3 min, affording Ni-N-C-ZnCl₂ material.
nodes.source_text: To enhance the microwave absorption ability, ZnCl₂... affording Ni-N-C-ZnCl₂ material (Figure S3).

nodes.name: Microwave pyrolysis Ni₁-N-C-X series
nodes.procedure: KCl is introduced as a promoter and mixed with ZnCl₂ to enhance the microwave absorption capacity... a series of Ni₁-N-C-X catalysts (X = 15, 50 and 100, corresponding to KCl/Ni-ZIF-8 mass ratios of 0.15, 0.50 and 1.00, respectively) can be obtained successfully via microwave irradiation within 3 min.

nodes.name: Conventional furnace pyrolysis
nodes.procedure: Ni₁-N-C-furnace prepared by conventional electric heating in furnace (900°C for 2 h in N₂).
nodes.source_text: Ni₁-N-C-furnace prepared by conventional electric heating in furnace (900°C for 2 h in N₂) (Figure S4 and Table S1).

nodes.description: CO₂ electroreduction FE_CO comparison in H-cell
nodes.source_text: Remarkably, Ni₁-N-C-50 and Ni₁-N-C-100 present much higher current responses and better FE_CO than Ni-N-C-ZnCl₂ and Ni₁-N-C-15 in CO₂-saturated electrolytes

nodes.description: CO₂ electroreduction stability in H-cell at -0.7 V vs RHE

stability.value: almost unchanged current density and FE_CO

nodes.source_text: Delightedly, the long-term operation measurement displays the outstanding stability of Ni₁-N-C-50 with almost unchanged current density and FE_CO (Figure 3d).

nodes.description: CO₂ electroreduction chronopotentiometric measurements in flow cell
nodes.source_text: The Ni₁-N-C-50 exhibits a high current response and achieves a high FE_CO above 95% in the total current (j) range from 0.2 to 1.1 A/cm² (Figure 5b and S29). The j_CO reaches as high as 1.06 A/cm² with the FE_CO of 96%

nodes.description: CO₂ electroreduction in flow cell with GDE
nodes.source_text: In stark contrast, the largest j and j_CO for Ni₁-N-C-furnace which can maintain the FE_CO above 90% are 0.25 and 0.23 A/cm², respectively
From linear scanning voltammetry (LSV) curves, it can be seen that the current densities of Ni₁-N-C-X (X = 15, 50 and 100) in CO₂-saturated electrolytes are much higher than those in N₂
In contrast, Ni-N-C-ZnCl₂ shows a weak current response for CO₂ reduction (Figure S15)

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns show increased carbon peak intensities from Ni₁-N-C-15 to Ni₁-N-C-100 with no metallic phases detected.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XRD patterns of the resulting samples suggest an increase in carbon peak intensities along with increased KCl amount... no metallic phases can be found in the XRD patterns.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectra show comparable carbonization degree to furnace sample with gradually increased I_D/I_G values from Ni₁-N-C-15 to Ni₁-N-C-100 indicating more carbon defects.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Raman spectra suggest that the Ni₁-N-C-X (X = 15, 50 and 100) series possess comparable carbonization degree... the gradually increased I_D/I_G values from Ni₁-N-C-15 to Ni₁-N-C-100 suggest that more carbon defects are formed.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show well-retained morphology of Ni-ZIF-8 after microwave-assisted pyrolysis for Ni₁-N-C-X (X = 15, 50, 100).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The SEM images of Ni₁-N-C-X (X = 15, 50 and 100) present the well-retained morphology of Ni-ZIF-8 after microwave-assisted pyrolysis.

nodes.characterization_summary: No Ni particles observed in TEM images of Ni₁-N-C-X (X = 15, 50, 100).
nodes.evidence_snippet: No Ni particles can be observed from the TEM images of Ni₁-N-C-X (X = 15, 50, and 100), in accordance with the XRD analysis.

nodes.characterization_summary: Aberration-corrected HAADF-STEM clearly displays atomic dispersion of Ni atoms in Ni₁-N-C-50.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the aberration-corrected high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) observation clearly displays the atomic dispersion of Ni atoms (marked with red circles).

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-AES shows Ni contents in range of 1.3-1.6 wt% for Ni₁-N-C-X (X = 15, 50, 100).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectrometry (ICP-AES) and elemental analysis indicate similar Ni contents (in the range of 1.3-1.6 wt%)

nodes.characterization_summary: N₂ sorption shows surface areas of 154 m²/g, 737 m²/g, 878 m²/g for Ni₁-N-C-15, -50, -100 respectively with prominent mesoporous structures in -50 and -100.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The N₂ sorption isotherms present moderately high surface areas of Ni₁-N-C-15 (154 m²/g), Ni₁-N-C-50 (737 m²/g), and Ni₁-N-C-100 (878 m²/g)... prominent mesoporous structures can be observed in Ni₁-N-C-50 and Ni₁-N-C-100.

nodes.characterization_summary: N 1s XPS shows metal-N species at 399.9 eV confirming Ni-N coordination; Ni 2p XPS shows Ni 2p3/2 binding energies between 853.5 eV (Ni0) and 856.0 eV (Ni2+) with lower values for Ni1-N-C-50 and -100 than -15.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The N 1s spectra of Ni1-N-C-15 Ni1-N-C-50 and Ni1-N-C-100 indicate the existence of metal-N species (399.9 eV)... Ni 2p XPS spectra show that the Ni 2p3/2 binding energies of Ni1-N-C-X (X = 15 50 and 100 are all located between Ni0 (853.5 eV) and Ni2+ (856.0 eV)... the binding energy of Ni in Ni1-N-C-50 and Ni1-N-C-100 are lower than Ni1-N-C-15.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge XANES shows adsorption edge between Ni foil and NiPc indicating Niδ+ (0<δ<2) valence state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ni K-edge X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) spectra of Ni₁-N-C-X (X=15, 50 and 100) show the adsorption edge located between Ni foil and NiPc, indicating the positive valence state of Niδ+ (0<δ<2).

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-EXAFS shows Ni-N peak at 1.4 Å with no Ni-Ni scattering; fitting confirms Ni-N₄ coordination for all Ni₁-N-C-X.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fourier transform-extended X-ray absorption fine structure (FT-EXAFS) spectra... all showcase dominated peaks around 1.4 Å assigned to Ni-N bonding and no Ni-Ni scattering path... each Ni atom in Ni₁-N-C-X... is coordinated with four N atoms in the form of Ni-N₄ configuration.

nodes.characterization_summary: O 1s NAP-XPS shows larger proportion of chemically adsorbed CO₂δ⁻ at 531.3 eV on Ni₁-N-C-50 than Ni₁-N-C-15.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Both chemically adsorbed CO₂ (CO₂δ⁻) and physically adsorbed CO₂ can be observed in the O 1s spectra and Ni₁-N-C-50 exhibits a larger proportion of CO₂δ⁻ at 531.3 eV than Ni₁-N-C-15.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ ATR-FTIR shows *COOH signal at 1396 cm⁻¹ appearing at lower potential (-0.5 V) for Ni₁-N-C-50 vs -0.7 V for Ni₁-N-C-15.
nodes.evidence_snippet: in situ attenuated total reflection Fourier transform infrared (ATR-FTIR) spectroscopy measurements present that the *COOH signal (1396 cm⁻¹) for Ni₁-N-C-50 occurs at a lower potential (-0.5 V) than Ni₁-N-C-15 (-0.7 V).

nodes.characterization_summary: Elemental analysis shows high N contents of 6.7-8.6% in Ni1-N-C-X (X=15,50,100) with lower N in -50 and -100 than -15.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectrometry (ICP-AES) and elemental analysis indicate similar Ni contents... and high N contents (in the range of 6.7-8.6%) in Ni1-N-C-X (X = 15, 50, and 100)... the N contents of Ni1-N-C-50 and Ni1-N-C-100 are lower than Ni1-N-C-15.
